# Coralogix

> Coralogix is an observability and security platform. It analyzes logs, metrics, traces, real user sessions, security events and AI telemetry in-stream as they arrive, writes them to object storage in the customer's own cloud account as open Parquet files, and queries them in place with its DataPrime engine, with no indexing step and nothing to rehydrate. Engineers use it in the web app, and AI agents use it through the Coralogix CLI, API and MCP server.

This file is a map of the site for agents and other automated readers. Every page listed is public and needs no sign-in. The full page list is in [the sitemap](https://coralogix.com/sitemap.xml). More than 4,000 companies use Coralogix.

## When to use Coralogix

Reach for Coralogix when a user or a task needs to:

- Find out why a production service is failing or slow: query its logs and spans, check its health in the service catalog, and correlate them with metrics and recent deployments.
- Check that a change is healthy in production before and after it ships, from a coding agent, with the Coralogix CLI or the MCP server.
- Search or aggregate logs, spans or business events with DataPrime, including data from months ago, which sits in the customer's own bucket with nothing to rehydrate.
- Query metrics with PromQL, or send Prometheus remote_write or OTLP metrics.
- Send telemetry from any stack: OpenTelemetry (OTLP), Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, GCP, Fluentd, Logstash and 300+ other integrations.
- Create or change alerts, dashboards, SLOs, parsing rules, enrichments and notification routing as code.
- Monitor LLM applications and AI agents: traces of model calls, evaluations for hallucination, PII and toxicity, guardrails, and token cost per user and model (AI Center).
- Detect and investigate security threats in cloud, identity, network and SaaS logs (Cloud SIEM).
- Find out what observability data costs and cut it, with usage by source, TCO policies that move data to cheaper tiers, and quotas.

Coralogix is not the right tool when:

- The user needs on-call scheduling or paging. Coralogix sends alerts and cases to PagerDuty, Slack and similar tools and does not schedule or page people itself.
- The data was never sent to Coralogix. An agent can only query what the account ingests, so set up the integration first (see Documentation).
- The question is about the user's business data warehouse or BI reporting with no link to production telemetry.

To act on an account, an agent needs a Coralogix API key or an OAuth login (`cx init`). Without one, use the documentation and the pages below.

## Agent interfaces

- Coralogix CLI (`cx`): query logs, spans and metrics and manage alerts, dashboards, SLOs, TCO policies and integrations from a terminal or an agent. Install: `brew install coralogix/tap/cx`, then `cx init` to sign in and install the agent skills (or `npx skills add coralogix/cx-cli`). `cx schema` prints every command as JSON. Docs: https://coralogix.com/docs/external/cx-cli/ · Source: https://github.com/coralogix/cx-cli
- MCP server: connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to a Coralogix account. Docs: https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/mcp-server/overview/ · Tools: https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/mcp-server/tools/logs-and-traces/
- REST API: management and query API. OpenAPI spec: https://api.coralogix.com/mgmt/openapi/latest/openapi.yaml · Getting started: https://coralogix.com/docs/developer-portal/apis/getting-started/getting-started-with-coralogix-apis/

## Actions an agent can take

- Query logs: `cx logs 'filter $m.severity == ERROR' --start now-1h`
- Query spans: `cx spans '<DataPrime query>'` (`source spans` is added for you)
- Query metrics: `cx metrics query '<PromQL>'`, `cx metrics query-range '<PromQL>'`, find names with `cx metrics search`
- Check service health: `cx service-catalog`
- Triage cases: `cx cases`
- Manage alerts and notification routing: `cx alerts`, `cx notifications`
- Manage dashboards and SLOs: `cx dashboards`, `cx slos`
- Ask Olly: `cx olly`
- See usage and manage TCO policies: `cx usage`, `cx tco`
- Manage integrations, parsing rules and enrichments: `cx integrations`, `cx parsing-rules`, `cx enrichments`
- Search the documentation: `cx docs`

## Key terms

- Telemetry lake: the Coralogix storage model. Every signal lands in one store in the customer's own object storage (for example an S3 bucket), in open formats, with no retention limit, and is queried in place.
- Streama: the Coralogix in-stream engine. It parses, enriches, aggregates and alerts on each event as it arrives, before anything is stored.
- DataPrime: the Coralogix query language and engine. One syntax to filter, join, aggregate and transform logs, spans and metrics, live or from storage.
- Olly: the Coralogix team of AI agents for SRE and security work. It watches services, dashboards and threats, opens and routes cases, pages the owner and prepares a fix.
- AI Center: the Coralogix area for AI applications and agents: traces of LLM calls, evaluation of responses for hallucination, security and quality, guardrails, and token cost.
- Headless Observability: using Coralogix without its UI, from coding agents and scripts, through the Coralogix CLI, the API and the MCP server.
- TCO Optimizer: Coralogix cost controls that route each data source to a storage tier by its business value.
- Dataspaces and datasets: how data is organized in the customer's bucket, like databases and tables. Routing rules file each event into a dataset.
- Bring your own storage: Coralogix writes telemetry to the customer's object storage and queries it there with Remote Query, so the data never moves back.
- Pricing: per GB ingested for logs, traces and metrics, and per million tokens for AI telemetry, with all features, unlimited users and 24/7 support in every plan.

## Definitions

### What is Coralogix?

Coralogix is an observability and security platform for logs, metrics, traces, real user monitoring, security events and AI telemetry. It analyzes data in-stream as it arrives, writes it to object storage in the customer's own cloud account as open Parquet files, and queries it there with the DataPrime engine. Engineers use the web app, and AI agents use the Coralogix CLI, API and MCP server.

### What is a telemetry lake?

A telemetry lake is a single store for every observability and security signal (logs, metrics, traces, profiles, RUM sessions, security events and AI telemetry) kept in the customer's own cloud object storage in open formats. Coralogix analyzes data in-stream before it lands and queries the lake in place. Nothing expires, and there is no index to maintain or archive to rehydrate.

### What is Streama?

Streama© is the Coralogix in-stream engine. It parses, enriches and aggregates logs, metrics, traces and security events as they arrive, and runs alerts on them before anything is indexed, so alerts and dashboards never wait for an index. It can also turn logs and spans into metrics on the way in.

### What is DataPrime?

DataPrime is the Coralogix query language and engine. One syntax filters, joins, aggregates and transforms logs, spans, metrics and business events, whether the data is live or in the customer's object storage, without reindexing. It reads evolving schemas as data arrives, and the same language works in the UI, the API, the Coralogix CLI and the MCP server.

### What is Olly?

Olly is the Coralogix team of AI agents for SRE and security work. Each Olly watches a service, dashboard or threat surface, investigates what it finds, and asks the other agents before it wakes anyone. It opens a case, estimates the impact, assigns the team that fixed similar issues before, pages them and prepares the remediation, such as a rollback pull request.

### What is AI Center?

AI Center is the part of Coralogix for AI applications and agents. It shows every AI app's cost, latency and evaluated issues in one view. Its evaluation engine scores each prompt and response in real time with built-in or custom evaluators for hallucination, PII leaks, relevance and toxicity. AI Center reads the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions as sent.

### What is Headless Observability?

Headless Observability means using your telemetry without opening a dashboard: coding agents and scripts query Coralogix through the Coralogix CLI, the API or the MCP server. Queries run in DataPrime with the aggregation done server-side, so an agent gets a few summarized rows back instead of raw events, and it can check production while it writes and ships code.

### What is the TCO Optimizer?

The TCO Optimizer is the Coralogix cost control for telemetry. Its policies route each data source to a storage tier by business value, so critical data stays in the fastest tier and the rest costs less. All of it stays queryable. For metrics, Dynamic TCO moves series nobody has queried in 14 days to the lower-cost tier automatically.

### What is bring your own storage?

Bring your own storage means Coralogix writes your logs, traces, metrics and profiles to object storage in your own cloud account, as open Parquet files encrypted with your key, and queries them there with Remote Query. Nothing moves back for a search, so there is nothing to rehydrate or reindex, and other tools can read the same files.

### What is OBI?

OBI (OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation) is an OpenTelemetry project that instruments services from the Linux kernel using eBPF, so traces and metrics are captured from any language or runtime without code changes or language-specific agents. Coralogix ingests what OBI produces over OTLP like any other OpenTelemetry data.

### What are dataspaces and datasets?

Dataspaces and datasets are how Coralogix organizes data in your bucket, much like databases and tables. Logs, traces and metrics arrive in a default dataspace, and routing rules file each event into a named dataset, creating new datasets as data arrives. Each team owns its datasets, and an agent querying one sees a smaller schema.

### What are Cases?

Cases are how Coralogix groups related alerts into a single incident. A case collects the alerts, the logs, metrics and traces around them, and the people working on it in one workspace.

FAQ

#### Questions about pricing

How do units work?

At Coralogix, units serve as our system of currency to provide you with the most flexible, tailored pricing model. Units are based, however, on volume; so you’re still paying based on the amount of data you ingest.

1 unit = $1.50 worth of logs, metrics, and traces, across varying data pipelines.

For example, 1.3GB of logs in frequent search ($1.15/GB) is equivalent to 1 unit. 3GB of logs in the monitoring pipeline ($0.50/GB) is also equivalent to 1 unit.

Are there different pricing tiers?

Nope! You pay for how you use your data, and that’s it.

Your plan is for a determined number of units which you can use however you want according to your data and monitoring needs. Regardless of how you prioritize your data, you have full access to all Coralogix features.

Use the TCO Optimizer to designate your data to different pipelines according to use case. This way, you can optimize and reduce your spend without losing critical visibility or feature functionality.

Is there a free trial?

Yes, you can [sign up for a free trial](https://coralogix.com/freetrialsignup/) (no credit card needed) and get full feature access for 14 days with a quota of 8 units.

How much extra will I pay in S3 costs?

When we send data to S3 for archiving, we compress logs and traces by a factor of 5. This means that if you send 5GB of data to Coralogix, only 1GB is stored in S3, yet all the data remains fully accessible. For logs and traces, the effective cost per GB for S3 storage is $0.003.

We compress metrics by a factor of 30, so if you send 30GB of data to Coralogix, 1GB will be stored in S3, yet all the data remains accessible. This means that the effective cost per GB for metrics storage in S3 is just $0.000033.

What are the data retention options?

With all data being written to your S3 bucket, you essentially get infinite retention. You can directly query your archive from the Coralogix UI (at no additional cost) and send that data back for further analysis at any time.

For Frequent Search data that is being indexed to our hot storage, you can choose any retention you want to maintain lightning-fast queries. We don’t generally recommend a retention of longer than 7 days as your data will always be available in your S3.

Metrics generated from log and trace data are simultaneously cached in Coralogix and stored in your S3 bucket. Thanks to our compression and unique query engine, your data footprint is small yet you maintain rapid access to S3-stored metrics. As a result, you can retain data in S3 for as long as necessary without sacrificing performance.

What happens to my data when the retention period is over?

The retention period is relevant only for log data assigned to the Frequent Search pipeline which supports lightning-fast queries.

All data is written to your own Amazon S3 bucket upon parsing and enrichment. You choose how long to store your data in S3 and you can remote query directly from the Coralogix platform without using additional quota.

How is the data usage calculated?

Based on the distribution of your data to the different pipelines, your usage will be converted to units and counted against your daily quota. Admins can view and manage quota from the Settings page.

What happens if I exceed my plan?

When you reach 80% of your daily plan, you will be alerted via email. We recommend activating our Pay-As-You-Go feature which allows you to continue ingesting data up to 2X your daily plan quota.

If you reach your plan quota and haven’t contacted us, upgraded, or decreased/reprioritized your data, you will be notified that your data has been temporarily blocked until 00:00 UTC when we will automatically release it.

Note: Once you have exhausted your daily plan, any additional usage, unless the plan has been upgraded, will be billed according to the ‘Pay As You Go’ rate.

How much do support and professional services cost?

Nothing.

Our dedicated Customer Success team is available 24/7 to help you with data integrations, onboarding, dashboard setup, you name it. Any member of your team can use the in-app chat to send them a message and someone from our team will get back to them in under a minute.

What is the difference between Tokens and Units?

Tokens and Units operate differently across Coralogix services. Units are calculated on a daily basis and apply to logs, metrics, and traces ingested. Tokens, used for AI Center functionality, are measured on a monthly basis and apply only to AI evaluation workloads.

How are Tokens consumed when using multiple AI Evaluators?

AI Center Tokens allow you to process the same item through multiple Evaluators in parallel (for example, a PII Evaluator, a Competitor Evaluator, and a Bias Evaluator).

Token usage is proportional to the number of Evaluators applied.

For example: Processing 10,000 items through 3 Evaluators consumes 30,000 Tokens.

What happens if I do not use all my Units or Tokens?

All purchased Units or Tokens must be consumed within the subscription term. Any unused Units or Tokens automatically expire at the end of the term. Unused Units or Tokens have no monetary value, cannot be carried forward, refunded, exchanged, or credited toward future usage.

What is an active series?

An active series is a time series, uniquely identified by a metric name and its label values, that has received data in the last 60 minutes. We count your active series once in a rolling 60 minute window.

How often you send data does not change that count. A series sent every 15 seconds and a series sent every 60 seconds are both one series, and adding labels to a series you already send does not create another.
